guide: Start here: open Start and type the household name, both partner names, your monthly amount and the example growth in the yellow cells.
Replace demo data, step 1: in Accounts list your own accounts (a card or loan balance is the amount owed) and clear the demo rows; a single adult lists fewer accounts and leaves partner 2 empty.
Replace demo data, step 2: in Net worth type one balance per account for each month you want; the monthly pages, shares and charts fill in by themselves.
Replace demo data, step 3: in Bills list each bill with the account it leaves from, and type your transfers; the Joint and Separate map and the payday plan follow.
Pay-day routine: move the transfer from the Payday Transfer Plan to the joint account, move personal spending money and type both in Transfers.
Weekly routine: look at Joint Account Cover and the Balances now page before the next payday.

Month-close routine, in this order: type every account balance in Net worth, run the Month-end Snapshot Check, read Net Worth Now and the Change Explainer, type statements in Balance check, print the Net Worth Statement.
The projection and the target tools use your monthly amount and an example growth rate: an example, not a forecast.
A single adult with one income and no children can use most sheets and leave partner 2 rows, personal spending money and shared accounts empty.
Use the 18 tools, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
Every verdict is an estimate from your numbers; any range shown is a typical range, check your own numbers.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearly renewal, your data stays with you and there is nothing to link or re-connect; you type or paste your own data. It works in Excel and Google Sheets with no macros.
What this is not: it is not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice.

listing.title: Net Worth Tracker Excel Template: Assets, Liabilities, Net Worth Projection, Joint and Separate Accounts, Payday Transfers
listing.headline: Track net worth by month and plan the joint account transfers
listing.description:
Know what you own and owe in one Excel workbook, for a couple, a family or a single adult. Type one balance per account each month and the workbook shows assets, liabilities and net worth by month, the change on last month and on last year, the share by account group and by owner, and which accounts moved net worth this month.

A projection from your monthly amount and an assumed yearly growth shows an example at three growth rates, with years to a net worth target and the monthly amount that reaches a level by a date. Every projection is an example, not a forecast.

The Joint and Separate map shows every bill by the account it leaves from. The Payday Transfer Plan gives each partner's transfer to the joint account on every payday and what is left to spend, Joint Account Cover compares the joint balance with the bills due before payday, and Personal Spending Money follows each partner's own account. Balance Reconcile checks the balances you typed from statements against the workbook.

18 tools, 12 printable sheets, 12 documents, 12 checklists and 34 ready text messages to partners, the grandparent, your bank branch, the payroll office and your tax preparer are included. This is part six of the Household Finance suite. A standard .xlsx workbook that works in Excel and Google Sheets, with no macros, no subscription and no bank links: you type or paste your own data. It is a household money kit, not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice. Every verdict is an estimate from your own numbers.
